description: The scoring and payout mechanism of the 600M retroactive distribution, stated in one place. NOTHING IS POSTED AND NOTHING IS ANCHORED: usage is counted on chain as it happens by UsageCounter, and RpgfMinter pays from those already-final numbers, so there is no root to post, no bond, no challenge and no formulaHash. The reward is UNIFORM (no tag, category or weight) and UNCAPPED; Sybil resistance is the two-sided LIVE ETH STAKE, not a formula lever — and since 2026-07-31 breadth itself counts only STAKED SELLERS, so every unit of the score's dominant term costs one live stake. This file is the normative PROSE statement of what the contracts compute, and the machine-readable `parameters` the off-chain mirror (sdk/src/rpgf) derives its constants from. The mirror exists for display and verification — recomputing what the chain already holds — never for posting an answer. Integer arithmetic throughout; no floating point anywhere.

parameterUnits.scoreScale: 10^18, the fixed-point scale inside the cube root so flooring error is negligible
parameterUnits.periodCount: The reference schedule (ruled 2026-07-31): nine ANNUAL accrual periods, ends at years 1..9 from RPGF_GENESIS. Per-period budgets group into three RISING tranches — 15% of the 600M over years 1-2, 30% over 3-5, 55% over 6-9, split equally within each tranche (45M/45M, 60M x3, 82.5M x4). Rising, because the largest share should pay on the most-measured evidence: the early network is the thinnest, most manipulable denominator, and early evidence-poor funding is the 300M DAO treasury's job. RpgfMinter validates its budget array against UsageCounter.periodCount() at deploy, so the two schedules cannot drift. Devnet rehearses the same nine-period structure at 30-minute periods.
parameterUnits.minSellers: UsageCounter.minSellers, the minimum-support floor (ruled 2026-07-31): a clause or assembly scores ZERO in a period until at least this many DISTINCT STAKED SELLERS have carried it there. Counting is never refused below the floor — c and d accrue, and the score springs whole when the floor is crossed. Below the floor sit exactly the clauses or assemblies one actor can fabricate alone: self-farms, fragmentation shards, squatted names, trivial riders. 3 is the smallest value at which solo or pair collusion cannot reach the scoreboard. A deploy-time immutable; devnet rehearses the mainnet value.

recording.call: UsageCounter.recordClauseUsage(order, clauseOrAssembly, sectionHash, proof) for a clause and UsageCounter.recordAssemblyUsage(order, compositionHash, proof) for an assembly (the provenance leaf derived from the compositionHash) — both permissionless; and, for trade settled in a proved batch, UsageCounter.applyBatchAccrual, callable only by FigaroBatchVerifier with values an immutable vkey committed. Only the section FINGERPRINT (keccak256 of the committed bytes) reaches calldata, never the preimage. The proof is what is trusted, never the caller; recording is gas-paid by whoever benefits, usually the clause or assembly's author.
recording.resolvedOrder: The order hash is recomputed from the signed Commitment struct and FigaroCore.orderStatus(orderHash) must equal 2 (RESOLVED). Usage is what a settled process leaves behind: an open process counts for nothing, and an unknown order reverts.
recording.sellerStake: SELLER-SIDE LIVE-STAKE GATE: the process's seller-of-record (order.seller) must hold a live MembersRegistry stake — MembersRegistry.registered(order.seller) must be true. An unregistered or withdrawn seller's settled trade does NOT count (SellerNotStaked). Since d counts distinct STAKED SELLERS (ruled 2026-07-31), this one gate prices breadth itself: n units of the score's dominant term cost n live stakes, linear, with no wallet-splitting leverage. Sybil resistance can only come from the cost of an identity — no scoring shape can separate a fabricated counterparty from a genuine one — so it is the registries' stake terms (deposit AND withdrawal cooldown) that carry it, never the formula.
recording.inclusion: The clause or assembly must be merkle-included in the order's signed agreementHash under AttestationCoordinator's leaf shape, byte for byte: keccak256(bytes.concat(keccak256(abi.encodePacked(clauseOrAssembly, sectionHash)))). The clause-or-assembly key is the ClauseRegistry idHash for a clause — keccak256(abi.encode(clauseId, version)) — or the AssemblyRegistry compositionHash for an assembly. There is no attestation and no article classification in the counting path; an assembly's credit rides its provenance leaf — the compositionHash committed in the agreement — which the counter derives and proves like any other leaf.
recording.period: Usage lands in UsageCounter.currentPeriod() — the first period whose end is still in the future. Once the last period has ended, accrual is closed forever and recordUsage reverts.
recording.idempotence: One process counts ONCE EVER per clause or assembly — globally, not per period — in whichever period it is first recorded; a repeat reverts (AlreadyCounted). A resolved order stays resolved and its struct is public, so a per-period key would let the same trade be re-recorded in every period: that pays for recording gas rather than adoption, and lets one fabricated period-0 farm be milked across every later period. Each period therefore counts only the usage that is NEW to it, which is what a fixed per-period budget schedule assumes.

accrual.c: Distinct settled processes that used the clause or assembly in the period.
accrual.d: Distinct LIVE-STAKED SELLERS of record across those processes in the period — incremented only on a seller's first counted process there. Until 2026-07-31 d counted (buyer, seller) pairs; pairs are the wrong statistic because they cannot be priced — the buyer side has no stake, so one staked seller plus N free buyer wallets was N units of the dominant term at gas cost, and even staking BOTH sides prices pairs sublinearly (k staked buyers times m staked sellers mint k*m pairs from k+m deposits). Distinct staked sellers is the leverage-free statistic: n units of breadth cost n live stakes, exactly linear, which is what the Sybil bound's rent-dissipation argument requires. (An earlier per-pair cap of 5 processes was deleted 2026-07-30 for the same family of reasons: it never bound the attacker and only bound honest repeat trade.)
accrual.score: score = icbrt(c * d * d * 10^18) when d >= minSellers, else 0 (and 0 when c = 0; d <= c by construction, so the two conditions never disagree), where icbrt is the floor integer cube root — i.e. c^(1/3) * d^(2/3) above the minimum-support floor. UNIFORM across clauses and assemblies: no tag, category or weight multiplier, so every clause or assembly's score is its real usage alone. Read it as score = d * (c/d)^alpha with alpha = 1/3: distinct staked sellers, times average repeat depth raised to alpha. Alpha is therefore the ELASTICITY OF REWARD TO REPEAT DEPTH (8x the depth earns 2x the score), and when every seller carries one process (c = d) the score is the count itself for any alpha. alpha < 1/2 is justified because a new relationship informs more than another observation of a known one; alpha = 1/3 exactly is a JUDGMENT, not a derivation, and it is uniform across clauses and assemblies so it is not curation. It is NOT a Sybil defense and is not offered as one — resistance lives in the cost of an identity, which is exactly why the statistic under the dominant exponent counts only staked identities. Value is deliberately not a term: the protocol's cost to move one unit equals its cost to move a trillion.
accrual.totalScoreIn: The period's summed clause-or-assembly scores, maintained in O(1) as a delta on every record. Final once the period ends. Scores are summed across the two settlement paths (scoreOf = direct + batch), never their components, and the minimum-support floor applies PER PATH — the counter holds the direct path's per-period seller set but only counts for the batched one, whose per-key seller sets the batch write does not carry, so it cannot union them. Summing scores over-counts a seller active on BOTH paths by a bounded factor (up to 2^(2/3) ≈ 1.59× the pooled figure at an equal split); flooring each side separately can only ever under-pay a boundary case, never let one seller straddle the universes.

payout.gate: RpgfMinter.claim(periodId, clausesOrAssemblies) requires UsageCounter.periodClosed(periodId): each period's budget pays for that period alone, whose counts stop moving the moment it ends. No snapshot, no checkpoint array, no history walk — and claims never expire, because a closed period's arithmetic is stable forever.
payout.authorOfRecord: Every passed clause or assembly is verified against its own registry with a LIVE stake — ClauseRegistry.depositOf(idHash) must have registeredBy == caller AND withdrawn == false; AssemblyRegistry.bindings(compositionHash) must have registeredBy == caller AND depositWithdrawn == false. This is the AUTHOR-SIDE half of the live-ETH-stake gate: you earn RPGF only while your clause or assembly's stake stays live. A clause or assembly the caller does not author, or whose stake is withdrawn, reverts (NotAuthorOfRecord). The caller's list is a lookup key, never a claim of ownership.
payout.entitlement: score = sum of the caller's clause-or-assembly scores for the period; amount = floor(periodAmount[periodId] * score / totalScoreIn(periodId)). THE CLAUSE-OR-ASSEMBLY LIST MUST BE DUPLICATE-FREE — a repeat reverts (DuplicateClauseOrAssembly). Until 2026-07-30 duplicates were summed and the total then CLAMPED to the period total, so any author of a non-zero-scoring clause or assembly could repeat it until the sum reached the denominator and mint the ENTIRE period budget; the clamp is what made it maximal, silently rounding a malformed claim up to the whole pool. With distinct clauses or assemblies score <= total holds structurally, so there is nothing to clamp. UNIFORM PRO RATA — no per-wallet cap. The reward tracks real usage directly, and the fixed pool is one a farmer dilutes, never inflates. Flooring dust stays unminted: the period amount is a ceiling, not a target.
payout.onceOnly: One claim per wallet per period — a wallet passes every clause or assembly it authored in that single call. The budget is enforced twice: RpgfMinter.minted[periodId] against periodAmount, and the outer FlorinToken minter cap registered at genesis.

reads.description: Everything the mirror needs is public chain state. Log order is (blockNumber, logIndex) ascending.
consumed: UsageCounter.UsageRecorded(bytes32 indexed clauseOrAssembly, uint8 indexed period, bytes32 indexed processId, address seller, uint64 c, uint64 d, uint256 score)

UsageCounter.BatchUsageRecorded(bytes32 indexed clauseOrAssembly, uint8 indexed period, uint64 c, uint64 d, uint256 score) — CUMULATIVE per clause-or-assembly-period; a later record replaces an earlier one
UsageCounter.accrualOf(clauseOrAssembly, period) / batchAccrualOf / totalScoreIn(period) / periodClosed(period) / minSellers()

MembersRegistry.MemberRegistered / MemberWithdrawalRequested — the seller-of-record's live-stake state (the seller-side gate, and with it breadth). De-surfacing is the REQUEST, not the later ETH release: eligibility ends when the member asks to leave, while the deposit stays locked for the withdrawal cooldown.
ClauseRegistry.ClauseRegistered — the clause's registeredBy of record (author-side gate reads depositOf.withdrawn)
AssemblyRegistry.AssemblyRegistered — the compositionHash's author of record
